subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: Robinson Crusoe and the Survival Narrative
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Robinson Crusoe and the Survival Narrative.

hook.text: In 1719, Daniel Defoe published a castaway story that many scholars consider the first English novel.

buildup.text: Robinson Crusoe survived alone on an island for twenty-eight years using only ingenuity and faith.

discovery.text: The novel was so realistic that many readers believed it was a true autobiographical account.

twist.text: Modern critics see the novel as a celebration of colonialism, with Crusoe claiming the island as his own.

climax.text: Robinson Crusoe invented the survival genre and shaped the Western myth of individual self-reliance.

punchline.text: One fictional castaway defined how the West sees itself.

quiz.question: Why do modern critics reexamine Robinson Crusoe?
options: They believe the writing quality is poor
They see it as a celebration of colonialism and self-serving conquest
They think the island was fictional
